messages:
incident-bot: 🔔 INCIDENT detected: Canary cluster eu-west-1 serving latency spike after deploy 1778009500. p50 +30%, p95 x4, throughput -40%. auto-alert created.

deploy-bot: CI/CD: rolled out release v2026.03.17 -> canary eu-west-1 at 1778009450. Changes: prefetch_fanout=high, batcher_window=8ms, kernel-selection tweak.

alan_eng_runtime: Seeing it live — canary p95 ~2.8s up from ~700ms. Batch queue depth jumping, KV cache hit rate stable tho.

raj_infra: CPU on GPU nodes is normal, but host-side batcher queues show lots of small microbatches stuck. suspect new batcher_window change.

sre_oncall: Confirmed customer-facing errors? Any 5xx or tool errors?

taylor_support: Not seeing 5xxs broadly yet but a few timed-out requests reported from Prod EU by account: "BrightDesk" and "ParcelFlow". Both on reserved Dedicated -> high priority.

maria_pm: @taylor_support estimate severity S2 for paying customers. Need mitigation plan now.

devx_jess: Can we flip the feature flag for prefetch_fanout or fallback kernel? Which is fastest?

alan_eng_runtime: fastest is kill-switch for prefetch fanout + reduce batcher_window back to 1ms. Command: 
```bash
# flip flag in config-service (staging path shown)
curl -X POST https://config.internal/flags/pretech_prefetch_fanout -d '{"value":0,"env":"canary-eu"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

raj_infra: I can run the flag flip and also trigger a canary rollback if needed. prepping the rollback command now.

deploy-bot: Rollout status: canary at 60% of eu-west-1 traffic. No automatic rollback triggered.

sre_oncall: Do the flag flip first. If latency not back in 5 minutes, rollback. I'll start tracing and open tcpdump on affected hosts.

raj_infra: flipped prefetch flag to 0 in canary-eu at 1778010080 :thumbsup:

alan_eng_runtime: watching metrics... p95 dropping from 2.8s -> 1.1s in 90s. throughput climbing. batch queue depth decreasing.

incident-bot: Update: latency improving after flag flip. Continue monitoring for 15m. Severity remains S2 while impact verified for 2 enterprise customers.

maria_pm: @taylor_support notify account reps: BrightDesk + ParcelFlow experiencing degraded response times earlier, now recovering. Provide ETA 30m and commit to postmortem.

taylor_support: Notifying now. I told both teams we're mitigating and will share postmortem.

devx_jess: Should we still roll back the full release or promote the fix to stable? pros/cons?

alan_eng_runtime: If flag flip holds across canary in 15m we can abort rollback and promote a targeted patch (batcher_window revert) to canary then stable. Rolling back full release causes churn for other regions.

raj_infra: I'll keep rollback command standing by: 
```bash
# rollback canary to previous revision
kubectl -n runtime rollout undo deployment/serving-canary --to-revision=1723
```

sre_oncall: Handoff: I'm staying until 1778013600 (approx 1h) to verify stability, after that handoff to next oncall @alan_eng_runtime for long-tail checks.

incident-bot: Pager log: paged oncall at 1778009999; escalation pinned to sre_oncall. Customers affected: BrightDesk, ParcelFlow (both EU). Initial mitigation: feature-flag flip; status: recovering.

maria_pm: Added customer-impact note to incident ticket INC-2026-314 at 1778010200. Will coordinate postmortem and communication timeline once stable.

taylor_support: Customers acknowledged. No open SLO breaches yet but we flagged for margin review.

alan_eng_runtime: Quick root-cause hypothesis: batcher_window increase caused more accumulation of small tokens into microbatches leading to kernel fallback thrashing under certain request size distributions in EU canary. Patch: revert batcher_window and add guard to avoid fallback under low-KV-hit conditions.

devx_jess: Recording the mitigation steps in the runbook: flip flag, monitor 15m, prepare rollback, notify customers.

incident-bot: Final update at 1778011100: p95 back to 750ms, throughput within -5% of baseline, no new customer reports. Marking as mitigated (monitoring). Keep thread open for postmortem notes.

raj_infra: I'll schedule a controlled canary patch with reverted batcher_window in 2 hours if stable.

maria_pm: Thanks team. @sre_oncall handoff acknowledged. I'll join postmortem sync in 2 hours.

sre_oncall: Handoff complete to alan_eng_runtime. Leaving logs and traces in INC-2026-314.

alan_eng_runtime: I'll pick up long-tail verification and prepare RCA draft.

incident-bot: Thread closed for active mitigation at 1778013600, reopened for postmortem updates.
